body.content: Counterfactual: Suppose the event log uses a Merkle mountain range rather than a linear hash chain. Resumption could verify log integrity in O(log n) rather than O(n). Would this change the resumability conditions? Likely not for the clean-halt requirement, but it would make tail-integrity validation cheaper, reducing the cost of the refusal-then-audit path for crash halts.
body.unfinished: Need to consider whether MMR-based logs change the partial-write detection semantics.
body.why_keep_this: Opens the question of whether log structure influences resumability policy beyond identity preservation.
